Understanding Vector Retrieval and Reranking

Retrieval augmented generation systems usually split the search problem into two stages. The first stage, vector retrieval, quickly narrows millions of documents down to a few hundred candidates using approximate nearest neighbour search over embeddings.

The second stage, reranking, spends far more compute per candidate. A cross-encoder reads the query and each candidate together and produces a precise relevance score, which is then used to reorder the shortlist before it is handed to the language model.

A minimal pipeline

The following snippet shows the two stages wired together. Notice that the reranker only ever sees the shortlist produced by the retriever, which keeps latency predictable.

const candidates = await index.search(embed(query), { topK: 200 });
const ranked = await reranker.score(query, candidates);
return ranked.slice(0, 5);

Trade-offs

StageLatencyPrecision
RetrievalLowMedium
RerankingHighHigh

In practice the best results come from tuning both stages together: a retriever with high recall gives the reranker something worth reordering, and a strong reranker lets you keep the retriever cheap.
